title: Port security, DHCP snooping and DAI

cards.heading: What port security does
cards.body: Port security limits which MAC addresses can send frames into a switch port and how many. It stops someone unplugging a desk PC and plugging in their own device, or flooding the MAC table.
cards.example:
interface fa0/3
 switchport mode access
 switchport port-security

cards.heading: Set the mode first
cards.body: Port security only works on static access (or trunk) ports. On a port left in the default dynamic mode, IOS rejects the command, so configure 'switchport mode access' first.
cards.example:
SW1(config-if)#switchport port-security
Command rejected: FastEthernet0/3 is a dynamic port.

cards.heading: Maximum and sticky addresses
cards.body: The default maximum is one MAC address. Sticky learning remembers the addresses it learns and writes them into the running configuration, so you don't have to type them in.
cards.example:
switchport port-security maximum 2
 switchport port-security mac-address sticky

cards.heading: Violation modes
cards.body: When an extra MAC address shows up: protect drops its traffic silently; restrict drops it, logs it and counts the violation; shutdown (the default) puts the port into err-disabled. Recover an err-disabled port with shutdown then no shutdown.
cards.example:
protect   drop                    port stays up
restrict  drop + log + counter    port stays up
shutdown  err-disabled            port goes down (default)

cards.heading: DHCP snooping
cards.body: DHCP snooping stops rogue DHCP servers. Every port is untrusted by default: the switch drops DHCP server messages (OFFER, ACK) that arrive on an untrusted port. Trust only the ports toward the real server. The switch also records each lease (MAC, IP, VLAN, port) in its binding table.
cards.example:
ip dhcp snooping
ip dhcp snooping vlan 10
!
interface g0/1
 ip dhcp snooping trust
!
show ip dhcp snooping binding

cards.heading: Dynamic ARP Inspection
cards.body: DAI stops ARP spoofing. On untrusted ports the switch checks each ARP message's sender MAC and IP against the DHCP snooping binding table and drops any that don't match. Trust the uplinks. DAI needs DHCP snooping (or static ARP ACLs) to have something to check against.
cards.example:
ip arp inspection vlan 10
!
interface g0/1
 ip arp inspection trust
